articles.title: Anthropic Releases Claude 4 with Extended Reasoning and 500K Context Window
articles.summary: Anthropic has officially launched Claude 4, featuring a 500,000-token context window and an enhanced extended thinking mode that allows the model to reason through complex multi-step problems. The new model reportedly outperforms GPT-5 on several coding and scientific benchmarks. Anthropic claims Claude 4 also incorporates new Constitutional AI 2.0 techniques to reduce hallucinations and improve factual grounding.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's AlphaFold 4 Predicts RNA and Protein-Ligand Interactions at Atomic Precision
articles.summary: Google DeepMind unveiled AlphaFold 4, expanding beyond protein structure prediction to accurately model RNA folding and protein-ligand binding interactions. Researchers say the system could dramatically accelerate drug discovery pipelines by predicting how candidate molecules interact with biological targets. Early access is being granted to pharmaceutical partners through a new commercial API.

articles.title: OpenAI Launches Operator Pro: Autonomous Web Agents Now Available to All ChatGPT Plus Users
articles.summary: OpenAI has expanded its Operator agentic platform to all ChatGPT Plus subscribers, enabling autonomous agents to browse the web, fill forms, book appointments, and execute multi-step tasks without human intervention at each step. The rollout includes new safety guardrails and a session-replay feature allowing users to audit agent actions. The move positions OpenAI directly against competitors like Google's Project Mariner and Cognition AI.

articles.title: EU AI Act Enforcement Body Issues First Major Fine to Meta Over Training Data Transparency
articles.summary: The newly established EU AI Act Enforcement Authority levied a €430 million fine against Meta, citing insufficient transparency disclosures about the datasets used to train its Llama 4 family of models. Meta has 60 days to appeal the ruling or submit a remediation plan. The decision is seen as a landmark test of the EU's willingness to enforce its sweeping AI regulations against major tech players.

articles.title: Microsoft Copilot Studio Gains RAG-Native Pipelines with Azure AI Foundry Integration
articles.summary: Microsoft announced that Copilot Studio now supports RAG-native pipeline construction directly within the Azure AI Foundry environment, allowing enterprise developers to build retrieval-augmented applications without writing custom orchestration code. The update includes automatic chunking strategies, hybrid search combining vector and keyword retrieval, and built-in evaluation dashboards. The feature is generally available starting today for Azure enterprise customers.

articles.title: Stanford HAI Report Warns Agentic AI Systems Pose Unprecedented Coordination Risks
articles.summary: Stanford's Human-Centered AI Institute published a comprehensive report arguing that the rapid deployment of multi-agent AI systems creates novel risks around unintended coordination, resource acquisition, and cascading failures that current safety frameworks are not equipped to handle. The report calls for mandatory sandboxing requirements and inter-agency communication logging standards before agentic systems are granted access to critical infrastructure. Several AI labs have already responded, with mixed reactions from the research community.

articles.title: Runway Gen-4 Video Model Achieves Cinematic-Quality Output at 4K Resolution
articles.summary: Runway has released Gen-4, its latest video generation model capable of producing 4K resolution, 60-second clips with consistent character identity across scenes. The model introduces a new temporal coherence architecture that eliminates the flickering and object drift that plagued earlier generative video tools. Hollywood studios including A24 and Warner Bros. are reportedly already piloting the technology for pre-visualization and concept development workflows.

articles.title: UC Berkeley Researchers Demonstrate LLMs Can Self-Correct Reasoning Errors via Iterative Debate
articles.summary: A new paper from UC Berkeley's BAIR lab shows that large language models can substantially reduce reasoning errors when two instances of the same model engage in structured adversarial debate, challenging each other's intermediate conclusions before producing a final answer. The technique, called Self-Adversarial Iterative Refinement (SAIR), improved accuracy on MATH-500 and GPQA benchmarks by up to 18 percentage points without any additional fine-tuning. The researchers have open-sourced the evaluation framework on GitHub.
